column2: Retain bringing, firm placement in David's tent and the two offering categories before God. Deliverance is the inherited rendering of the second offering term and does not introduce a separate narrative rescue.
Retain David finishing the offerings before blessing the people in the Lord's name. The shared offering vocabulary connects with verse 1 without merging the two acts.
Retain distribution to every Israelite, explicitly men and women, and one baker's loaf plus a cake for each. The selected clause does not include a separate meat portion.
column3: The precise kind of amorites cake and the force of artokopikos require lexical review; no raisin, date or meat ingredient is asserted.

column2: Retain Levites appointed before the covenant ark for ministry, sounding out, thanksgiving and praise. The list introduces the personnel in the next unit rather than a new independent speech.
Retain Asaph's leadership, Zacharias second, the three occurrences of Jiiel and all intervening names. Harps and lyres specify instruments; Asaph's cymbal sounding is separately stated.
column3: Instrument nomenclature remains provisional, and repeated Jiiel is not silently deduplicated.

column2: Retain Banaias and Oziel as priests, trumpets, continual activity and the ark of God's covenant. Do not harmonize the priest roster with the preceding procession chapter.

Retain David's initial appointment of praise through Asaph and his brethren on that day. The inherited formulation leaves the appointment at the beginning without asserting that no earlier praise ever occurred.

Retain thanksgiving and calling upon Him by His name, followed by making His works known among peoples. Two display lines follow the selected poetic clauses; the imperatives address worshippers, not God.

Retain singing and hymning to Him, recounting to everyone and the closing which the Lord has done. The selected additional relative clause is not shortened to the parallel psalm's familiar wording. Two lines distinguish singing from recounting.

Retain praise in His holy name and the singular heart seeking His good pleasure. Do not substitute seekers of the Lord or make the future rejoicing another imperative. Display separates the two clauses.

Retain seeking the Lord and becoming strong, followed by continually seeking His face. Be strengthened is a provisional idiomatic rendering of the strength imperative, not a claim that the Greek is passive. Two lines preserve the repeated seek.
Retain remembering His performed wonders and the further portents and judgments of His mouth. The sentence continues into its addressees in verse 13; two lines retain that movement.
Retain offspring of Israel, His servants, and sons of Jacob, His chosen ones. Do not replace Israel with Abraham from a parallel psalm. Two lines display the paired descriptions of those addressed.
Retain the identification as the Lord our God and judgments throughout all the earth. Two nominal clauses are made readable with supplied English copulas, without narrowing earth to one territory.
Retain He remembers, for the selected participle describes the Lord rather than commanding the people to remember. His covenant and His word for a thousand generations remain in two lines.
column3: The relation of the participle to the preceding identification and of word to covenant merits syntactic review; the English finite verb supplies continuity.

column2: Retain establishment with Abraham and His oath to Isaac. The relative clause continues the preceding covenant-word construction; display separates Abraham and Isaac without supplying a new covenant event.
Retain establishing it for Jacob as an ordinance and for Israel as an everlasting covenant. Two lines retain the paired names and predicates rather than presenting two different recipients.

Retain the divine promise of Canaan and the measured inheritance allotment, with two display lines. Initial you is singular and your inheritance is plural in Greek; ordinary English you/your does not visibly distinguish them.
column3: The singular-to-plural change is recorded here; no ye or explanatory expansion is inserted into the reading text.

column2: Retain their becoming few in number, being made small and sojourning in the land. Third-person they is selected, not a harmonized second-person you. Two lines preserve the temporal and comparative clauses.
column3: The relation of as they were made small to few in number remains open; no merely or very is added.

column2: Retain nation to nation and kingdom to another people. Two lines preserve the changing collective nouns instead of regularizing both halves to kingdoms or nations.
Retain the prohibition of any man overpowering them and rebuke of kings on their account. Two lines lead into the quoted prohibitions; no physical punishment of the kings is added.
Retain plural anointed ones and prophets, each with its own prohibition. Two lines retain the parallel commands and divine first-person possession; no singular messianic referent is substituted.

Retain the whole earth addressed to sing and proclaim salvation day by day. Two lines follow the selected poem. The stored sequence moves directly to verse 25: verse 24 is absent and is not imported from a parallel witness.
Retain the Lord's greatness, abundant praiseworthiness and fearsome supremacy over all the gods. Two lines distinguish praise from fear; no verse 24 material is placed in this unit.
Retain the nations' gods as idols and our God as maker of singular heaven. Two lines preserve the contrast; no earth is supplied to make a familiar creation formula.
Retain glory and praise before Him, strength and boasting in His place. Two lines preserve the paired nouns; boasting is not silently changed to beauty or joy.
column3: The best restrained English rendering of kauchema here remains a lexical and literary question.

column2: Retain ancestral families of the nations and the repeated give to the Lord. Two lines distinguish the summons from its objects, glory and strength, without reducing families to individual worshippers.
Retain glory of His name, plural gifts brought before Him and worship in His holy courts. Three lines follow these clauses; the selected courts are not replaced with holiness or holy attire.
Retain the whole earth's fear, the earth being set right and its not being shaken as commands or wishes. Two lines preserve the mood; no assertion that the world is already immovable is substituted.
Retain heaven's gladness, earth's exultation and the plural proclamation among the nations that the Lord reigns. Two lines distinguish cosmic rejoicing from the proclamation.

Retain future resounding of the sea with its fullness, singular tree of the field and everything in it. Two lines preserve the selected unusual tree/field construction rather than importing a field rejoicing clause.
column3: The grammatical reach of resound and the antecedent of in it remain unresolved; singular tree is deliberate.

column2: Retain the forest's plural trees rejoicing before the Lord because He has come to judge the earth. Two lines preserve the causal relation and the selected arrival tense.
Retain for it is good, following the selected neuter adjective, rather than silently replacing it with He is good. Two lines distinguish the thanksgiving exhortation from enduring mercy.
column3: Whether the neuter evaluates thanksgiving or functions idiomatically of divine goodness remains a question for specialist review.

column2: Retain Save us and rescue us from the nations, followed by praise of Thy name and glorying in Thy praises. Four lines display the invocation and purposes. Thy is restricted to this direct prayer to God; no gathering clause is imported.

Retain blessing from age to age, the people's future Amen and their past praise. Three display lines keep the final narrative praise distinguishable from the doxology; do not turn shall say into a completed said.
Retain plural they left Asaph and his brethren, continual service and each day's duty on its day. The selected plural agent is not silently changed to David alone.
Retain Abdedom with sixty-eight brethren, then Abdedom son of Idithon and Ossa as gatekeepers. The repeated name is not collapsed into one occurrence.
column3: The scope of sixty-eight and the relation of the two Abdedom mentions need genealogical review; the text does not identify them as certainly one or two men.

column2: Retain Sadok and his brother priests, the Lord's tent and Bama in Gabaon. They left is supplied from the preceding construction to support English continuity.
column3: Bama remains an inherited place-like form; whether it should instead be rendered as the high place is unresolved.

column2: Retain continual whole burnt offerings morning and evening, conformity to the written law and God's command through Moses His attendant. All these clauses belong to the appointment purpose, not a fresh claim of completed offerings.
Retain singular with him, Aiman and Idithon, the remaining named chosen men and enduring mercy as the praise rationale. The selected singular attachment is not regularized to with them.
column3: The antecedent of with him remains open within the extended personnel list.

column2: Retain plural with them, trumpets, cymbals, instruments for God's songs and Idithon's sons at the gate. The selected sentence has no repeated Aiman and Idithon names to insert.
Retain the people each going home and David returning to bless his household. Do not append the dispute with Melchol from a parallel narrative.
